articles.title: Cult venue Prince Charles cinema ‘saved’ after lease renewal signed
articles.summary: The much-loved central London institution, which has been threatened with closure since January 2025, secures 25-year lease without break clause with current landlords.
body: The celebrated Prince Charles repertory cinema in London’s Leicester Square has announced that the threat of closure has been staved off by signing a new 25-year lease with its landlords.

In a post on social media titled “You Saved the PCC”, the cinema said that “after 21 months of uncertainty, we’re delighted to have secured the future of the cinema” and that they had “signed a new 25-year lease with no break clause, ensuring our projectors will keep rolling for years to come”.
The cinema also expressed its gratitude for the “support, commitment and belief of many, many people”.

In January 2025, the Prince Charles launched a petition, claiming that its landlord, Zedwell LSQ Ltd (owned by developer Criterion Capital) was trying to “bully us out of the building” by demanding a break clause in its lease, due for renewal in September 2025. The break clause would have enabled Zedwell to give the cinema six months’ notice if it had other plans for the site. At the time, Criterion Capital denied that it was attempting to intimidate or disadvantage the cinema.
points: The much-loved central London institution, which has been threatened with closure since January 2025, secures 25-year lease without break clause with current landlords.

articles.title: ‘Stranger than stranger-than-fiction’: how Lance Oppenheim made the year’s two buzziest films
articles.summary: Primetime and You Can See Everything are both clammy, audacious awards contenders that challenge our sense of reality. Ahead of the release of his drama starring Robert Pattinson as a TV vigilante, the 30-year-old director talks crime, punishment and South Park.
body: When I meet Oppenheim in a London hotel, it is to discuss his other hot ticket, Primetime, for which Robert Pattinson is the one attracting Oscar buzz. The Batman actor gives a high-wire performance as Chris Hansen, the sensationalist US television vigilante renowned for ambushing paedophiles on To Catch a Predator, which was a disreputable and highly addictive segment of the current affairs show Dateline NBC between 2004 and 2007. Hansen later parlayed the idea, and his crusading shtick, into a succession of spin-offs. Some, including Hansen Vs Predators, had the same sleazy catnip quality. Others, such as a sting to collar bicycle thieves, did not.

articles.title: ‘Don’t do this!’ Why Paul McCartney cares about looking shorter than John Lennon in Sam Mendes’ Beatles films
articles.summary: You’re Paul McCartney. So how come you’re still getting het up at a fictional version of you being marginally smaller than a fictional version of John Lennon? There has been a lot of discourse and conjecture surrounding Sam Mendes’s forthcoming Beatles biopics.
body: But until now the remaining Beatles have managed to keep fairly quiet about the whole thing. Last year Ringo Starr mentioned that he’d sat down with Mendes to rework a scene he wasn’t happy with, and Paul McCartney has praised the guitar playing of Paul Mescal, but it appeared that no real red lines had been crossed. Until now.

On the most recent episode of Amy Poehler’s podcast, McCartney hinted at one underlying tension that might just rip the whole project apart: under no circumstances should he be seen to be shorter than John Lennon.

Informing Poehler that he, Lennon and George Harrison were all roughly equal height – with Starr slightly smaller – McCartney revealed that he was moved to text Mendes after shots of the actors recreating the Abbey Road album cover were published. In them, it looked an awful lot like Harris Dickinson (playing Lennon) loomed above Mescal’s McCartney. As per McCartney’s retelling, the text read “Sam! Smaller? Don’t do this! You said you wouldn’t do it!”

articles.title: ‘Love of Your Life’ Director Rachel Morrison on Margaret Qualley’s ‘Wild Range,’ Confronting COVID-19 and Subverting Romantic Drama Expectations: ‘Finding Herself Is Enough’
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This post contains spoilers for “Love of Your Life,” now streaming on Prime Video. When Rachel Morrison read the script for “Love of Your Life,” it stuck with her.
body: “I obviously was drawn to the script, but didn’t immediately think, ‘This is my next project,'” Morrison tells Variety over Zoom. “It really was just, this is good writing and I want to talk about it with this writer.”

Morrison and Cox really connected. “There was a deep sense of mutual respect, but also, for this script that was incredibly well received and jumped off the page, she was not precious about it,” Morrison says. “The more I sat with it, the more it sort of got under my skin.”

The same was true for the film’s cast, an all-star ensemble led by Margaret Qualley as Maya and including Gabriel Basso as Charlie; Aaron Pierre as Felix, a handsome stranger she meets abroad; Patrick Schwarzenegger as her best friend Jason; and Catherine Keener in a scene-stealing performance as Charlie’s mother Ruth.
“We have leading actors playing supporting roles, and I think that’s because this really spoke to them,” Morrison says.

articles.title: ‘La Bola Negra’ Soundtrack Features New Music From Composer Raül Refree
articles.summary: “La Bola Negra” soundtrack, featuring music by composer Raül Refree, is set to be released on Oct. 16 by Lakeshore Records. Taking its name from an unfinished play by Lorca and drawing on his writings and legacy, “La Bola Negra” is directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi better known as Los…
body: It’s an intense score that grows along with the film and with the different protagonists as their stories unfold.

Refree, who is one of Variety’s 10 artisans to watch, tied his instrumentation to the characters rather than the eras. “Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) plays the trumpet, so his scenes rely heavily on the brass section. Carlos (Milo Quifes) plays the piano, so his music features the piano alongside the string section. Finally, Alberto’s (González) story takes place in the present day, and because he is going through a personal crisis, his music relies much more on silence,” Refree says.

As the film progresses and the paths of the three protagonists cross in one way or another, the timbres and instrumental approach also begin to blend. “Mira que nos acechan” is where all the concepts come together, carrying the meaning that we are all one.

articles.title: Bollywood Actor Imran Khan Heads to High Court to Fight Order to Leave India Over Election Protest
articles.summary: Imran Khan is preparing a court challenge to an order that gives the Bollywood actor until Oct. 28 to leave India, after he attended a demonstration demanding that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar step down.
body: Police rounded up upwards of 400 people across Mumbai on Oct. 10, many of them at August Kranti Maidan, where demonstrators had gathered in solidarity with a Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest in Delhi. The Delhi agitation centers on allegations that voter lists were manipulated during the Special Intensive Revision exercise. According to police, nobody had sought permission for the Mumbai event, and Azad Maidan is the sole venue where the Bombay High Court permits protests in the city.
Speaking to reporters before he was detained, Khan said he had no demands. “I am here as a citizen, as someone who lives in this city,” he said.

Police also picked up his girlfriend, actor Lekha Washington, and his cousin Zayn Marie Khan. From inside the van, Khan shared an Instagram selfie captioned “Apparently I’m going for a drive.” He had also taken part in CJP’s July demonstrations.

articles.title: Guillermo del Toro Pays Tribute to Late ‘E.T.’ Designer Carlo Rambaldi Ahead of Hollywood Walk of Fame Honor: ‘A Worldwide Maestro of Magic’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Guillermo del Toro is paying tribute to Italian special effects master Carlo Rambaldi, who is being honored today with a posthumous Hollywood Walk of Fame star. Rambaldi, best known for designing the iconic title character in Steven Spielberg’s “E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial,” died in 2012 at age 86.
body: Rambaldi was born in the village of Vigarano Mainarda, outside the city of Ferrara, in the northern Italian region of Emilia-Romagna. The son of a bicycle mechanic, he graduated from the Academy of Fine Arts in Bologna in 1951 and, though he dreamed of becoming an artist, was drawn into the world of cinema when he was asked to create a dragon for a low-budget science fiction movie in 1956.
Del Toro has been known to share a deep passion with Rambaldi for creatures used in contemporary fantasy and horror cinema made through the artisanal use of animatronics.

“Carlo Rambaldi changed the world of special effects, makeup and puppetry,” del Toro says in a video message shared exclusively with Variety. “He brought a know-how and a finesse and a great sense of character and design that can only be described as being the heir of the old world craftsmanship and beauty that comes with a country with a great theatrical tradition and a great artistic tradition.”

Del Toro added: “Without him, it’s absolutely impossible to imagine the daring, beautiful work that is being done now and in the last few decades. He is not only a great Italian effect master, but a worldwide maestro of magic.”

articles.title: Wallace & Gromit maker Aardman falls short of return to profit
articles.summary: Animation studio narrows annual loss to £1.1m amid ‘challenging market’ in children’s content. Don’t break out the celebratory Wensleydale just yet. Aardman, the British animation studio behind the cheese-loving inventor Wallace and his beloved dog Gromit, has fallen short of a target to get back…
body: The employee-owned business was aiming to record a small profit in 2025 after two years of consecutive losses but was hit by production delays and a “challenging market” in children’s content.
So although its revenues jumped 8% to £20.4m last year, it was in the red to the tune of £1.1m, albeit an improvement on the previous year’s £4.1m loss.
Aardman, which also produces the popular Shaun the Sheep series, said the timing of some “significant” deals and weaker income in some parts of the business had hurt its bottom line.

It will be hoping for a boost from new projects, such as a recently opened exhibition at Lightroom in London that explores its 54-year history, as well as a third Shaun the Sheep film, which was released last month.

articles.title: Nandy 'minded to intervene' in Sky's £1.6bn takeover of ITV entertainment arm
articles.summary: The culture secretary says the deal could affect free expression in the media and the variety of Britain's news landscape.
body: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has said she is "minded to intervene" in the proposed £1.6bn deal for Sky to buy ITV's media and entertainment division.
Sky said it would "carefully consider" a letter from the culture secretary and "engage constructively" with the review into the deal.
"We remain confident that bringing Sky and ITV's media and entertainment business together will create a stronger British media," it said.
ITV welcomed the letter and said the deal would help it "compete with global streaming platforms, benefiting viewers, advertisers and the UK creative industries".

articles.title: Russell Brand accuser says alleged rape left her afraid she may be pregnant
articles.summary: The 51-year-old faces three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.
body: A woman who alleges Russell Brand raped her in a hotel has said she was left feeling "dirty" and afraid she may be pregnant in the aftermath of the alleged attack.
The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies the charges.
Video evidence played to the jury at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday showed one of his complainants tell the police: "He raped me basically and I know that happened."
The jury heard one of Brand's accusers say she had met him in 1999, before he was famous.

articles.title: Ralph Fiennes to Star In, Executive Produce ‘Unbeaten’ Racehorse Drama for ‘Conclave’ Producer, StudioCanal
articles.summary: He will play Sir Henry Cecil, the legendary horse trainer, with 'Outrun' director Nora Fingscheidt to helm the theatrical feature set to shoot in 2027.
body: Ralph Fiennes is set to star in and executive produce Unbeaten, a theatrical feature from Conclave producer House Productions, StudioCanal and Escapade Pictures.

The theatrical feature in advanced development is based on screenplay by Bash Doran and will be directed by BAFTA winner Nora Fingscheidt ( Outrun ). “I knew nothing about the legendary Henry Cecil until I read Bash Doran’s screenplay. I was compelled and moved by it and by Henry’s story with the great horse Frankel. Henry was — and still is — a unique figure, complex and competitive in the very specific world of horse racing,” Fiennes, who received an Oscar nomination for his performance in Edward Berger’s Vatican-set drama. said in a statement.
His other credits include Wuthering Heights, Quiz Show, The English Patient, Schindler’s List, In Bruges, The Grand Budapest Hotel and The Menu.

The film reunites Fiennes with House Productions’ Tessa Ross, who also produced Conclave. Rory Aitken of Escapade Pictures and 42 will also produce. StudioCanal is fully financing the project, handling worldwide sales and is set to release Unbeaten in the U.K., France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Benelux, Australia and New Zealand.
